newsitem.title: USA: Dow surges as bonds rally, NYSE sets trading curbs.
newsitem.headline: Dow surges as bonds rally, NYSE sets trading curbs.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks roared higher on Friday as the long bond rallied following the release of U.S. unemployment data in May which gave ambiguous signals about the strength of the labor market.

The Dow industrial average soared over 100 points then backed off to trade up around 88 points, or 1.42 percent, at 7395. The New York Stock Exchange set curbs on index-arbitrage trading at 1115 EDT/1515 GMT.
The long bond, which initially tumbled on the data, traded up 16/32 at a 6.84 percent yield.
Nasdaq also made a decisive break to higher ground after waffling much of the morning session. It was trading up around five points or 0.32 percent at 1395.

"The bond market has decided that the employment data is positive," said Douglas Cliggott, U.S. equity strategist at JP Morgain. "Bonds have surged in the last half hour or so and equities have followed right along in their path."
The rebound in the Treasury bond market was also attributed to some short-covering.
The Labor Department said the unemployment rate fell in May to 4.8 percent, but with only 138,000 new jobs added.
